113 ft ground to ventilating ball (nomination) versus 90 ft in the 1894 Board description and the USLHS record (base to lantern center). The sources measure different things or disagree.

notes_for_editor: Newspaper searches (Chronicling America, Illinois papers, 1873-80, 1924, 1930-35) returned no hits, so no newspaper is cited. Lighthouse Board annual reports for 1873-1890 are not in the local corpus; the construction story rests on the NHL nomination and LighthouseFriends (which follows Terras). Disagreements left stated in the text: Moore's age at death (73 vs 69), Lady Elgin dead (300 vs 400), lens date (1850 vs 1860), foundation depth, tower height (113 vs 90 ft), electrification (1923 vs 1934), cost ($35,000 appropriated vs $55,000 to establish), whistles date (Board FY1892 text says 9 April 1891 while FY1891 table still lists sirens). Fog-signal hours were read from OCR tables by entry number (452 in the FY1900 report, 472 in FY1901); the FY1901 text prints the state of entry 472's heading garbled ('Michigan') for the Grosse Point sound-deflector line; it is matched to Grosse Point, Illinois by its position between Chicago Harbor (470) and Waukegan (473). Byron B. Palmer is matched to Hagan's 'Mr. Palmer, 2nd Asst.' by surname, rank and year. The 1894 'about 504 hours' and other fog-hour figures in the volume's FY1893 and FY1894 sections were not used because they conflict with each other. The nomination's date of 1 March 1874 comes from its endnote citing Hyde. Visitor details come from the lighthouse's own site (undated, 'subject to change'). Position: the record's coordinates (42.0639, -87.6760) agree with USLHS within 0.06 km.
